summary: Lists AI-specific review hazards (automation bias, vigilance decrement, code-quality erosion, ~40% vulnerable suggestions, package hallucination/slopsquatting), then presents nine re-presentation techniques in three tiers: spec-before-code, AI self-explanation with a least-confident section, tests as specs; risk-tiered ~200 LOC chunks, layered summaries, diagrams; back-translation, adversarial second model, review-friendly prompting. Closes with 2025-2026 industry workflows (Google SRE, Anthropic, GitHub) and the EASE 2026 AIDev review-comment breakdown.

claims.text: Hallucinated 'huggingface-cli' PyPI package received over 30,000 downloads in three months (Lasso Security)
19.7% of generated packages fictitious across 16 LLMs and 576,000 samples; commercial 5.2% vs open-source 21.7% (USENIX Security 2025)
2026 re-evaluation: frontier models still hallucinate packages at ~4.6-6.1%; 127 names invented identically by five models
Google SRE: line-by-line review does not scale with 4x-10x code volume; oversight must move up the abstraction ladder
Of human comments on AI-authored PRs, 64.53% were direct review, 28.37% agent steering, 7.10% CI (EASE 2026, AIDev >932k PRs)
claims.anchor: L84 '64.53% were direct human review' vs L84 '65.53% direct review'

claims.text: Test-defining agent must be isolated from code-generating agent to prevent cross-bias (Google SRE guidance)

risks.note: Direct-review share stated as 64.53% and 65.53% in the same paragraph; one is wrong.
'Churn roughly doubling' has no figure or source beyond GitClear label.
Back-translation 'divergence localizes bugs' and mutation-consistency backbone cite no study.
'Anthropic's own usage data shows' users shift to monitoring; no report named.

least_confident: The EASE 2026 percentages, since the paragraph gives two different direct-review figures and I cannot tell which the source reports.
